standard_prerequisites.name: Largest open of the base on which a tau-locally checked morphism property holds, with its characterization over coverings (Descent chapter, Lemma descent-lemma-largest-open-of-the-base, canonical tag 06QP)
standard_prerequisites.use: Used twice: it gives the maximal open W for s|_{s^{-1}(W)} and, applied over the tau-coverings {s} and {t} with the fibre product square of the groupoid diagram, identifies t^{-1}(W) = W_1 = s^{-1}(W).

core_obligations: The open W exists with its maximality property by descent-lemma-largest-open-of-the-base. In the groupoid diagram (equation carried as context) let W_1 be the maximal open subscheme of R over which pr_1 : R x_{s,U,t} R to R has P. The square of the diagram exhibits pr_1 over W_1 as the base change of s : R to U by t restricted appropriately; since P is tau-local on the target and {t : R to U} is a tau-covering, descent-lemma-largest-open-of-the-base gives t^{-1}(W) = W_1. Symmetrically, using the covering {s : R to U} and the other projection pr_0, the same lemma gives s^{-1}(W) = W_1. Hence t^{-1}(W) = s^{-1}(W), which by the definition of R-invariant opens means W is R-invariant.
proof_roadmap: Take W and its characterizing maximality from descent-lemma-largest-open-of-the-base (proof lines 665-666).
Define W_1 as the maximal open of R for pr_1 in the groupoid diagram carried as context (proof lines 667-670).
Apply the same Descent lemma over the tau-coverings {t} and {s} to get t^{-1}(W) = W_1 = s^{-1}(W), i.e. R-invariance of W (proof lines 671-674).
